verdicts.claim: 13.04.02 specifies a caveated wider range for low confidence, which 13.04.03 D-01/DT-01 forbid and 13.04.02's own D-02 contradicts.
verdicts.reason: Quote verified verbatim (13.04.02-pricing-suggestions-repricing.md:53 `| Partial | Low confidence | Wider range, prominent caveat, or withheld entirely per 13.04.03 |`), and 13.04.03-valuation-confidence-thin-market.md:63 does reject caveating. But the cell is not a specification — it delegates in terms (`per 13.04.03`), and 13.04.02 subordinates itself to 13.04.03 twice more in the same file: :65 'Gated by 13.04.03 Valuation Confidence — no confidence, no suggestion' and :77 D-02 'No confidence, no suggestion — silence over fabrication'. 13.04.03:57 and :32 give the concrete render (raw comps as examples, no median, no suggestion) and 13.04.03:69 states the gating direction reciprocally. An implementer following the cell's own pointer lands on the only permitted rendering; there is no forced invention and no statement that governs against another. Residual defect is stale enumeration inside a delegating cell (the words 'prominent caveat' should not survive DT-01) — a wording cleanup, not an ambiguity: rule 5 convergence and rule 3 answer-is-elsewhere both apply.

verdicts.claim: gear-marketplace-cx.md gives CX-M11 two mechanism identities eight lines apart and routes message-to-disclosure promotion to the wrong cross-cut (messaging is CX-M06 everywhere else).
verdicts.reason: Both rows verified verbatim: gear-marketplace-cx.md:382 '| **Step 6:** Message-to-disclosure promotion | **CX-M11** Messaging & Conversations |' and :390 '| **CX-M11** Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport | Does not serve gear-marketplace...'. The second label is canonical and corroborated outside this domain — 13.05.02-auctions-bidding.md:71 'Consumes **CX-M11 Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport**', plus the same label in 20-fanbase-direct-to-fan (20.05.06 / fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md). Messaging is CX-M06 in this domain without exception: 13.05.01-offers-counter-offers.md:127 'Consumes **CX-M06 Messaging & Contextual Inbox**', 13.06.02-order-management-lifecycle.md:166 'Consumes **CX-M06 Messaging**', 13.12-gear-seller-storefront-policies.md:41 '| Contact / follow | CX-M06 / CX-M28 |'. So one ID carries two mechanisms in one file, and the row that assigns work to CX-M11 sits eight lines above the row recording that CX-M11 does not serve this domain. The product behaviour (one-tap promotion of a message claim into structured disclosure, 13.02.02:101/:131 DT-12) is fully specified, so nothing product-level is invented — this is a cross-reference-integrity defect that mis-targets the cross-cut wiring and leaves CX-M06 unnotified of the promotion obligation. Warning is the right severity.

verdicts.claim: 13.02.02 declares a dependency on CX-M11 for messaging, but CX-M11 is Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport; the mechanism it needs is CX-M06.
verdicts.reason: Verified verbatim at 13.02.02-mandatory-flaw-disclosure.md:155 '- **Consumes CX-M11 Messaging** — DT-12: condition claims made in messages are promotable to structured disclosure.' The same file makes a second wrong-ID reference at :93 ('Routes to moderation (CX-M11/domain 24)'). CX-M11's canonical identity is Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport (13.05.02-auctions-bidding.md:71, and the identical label in domain 20), and the messaging mechanism is CX-M06 (13.05.01:127, 13.06.02:166, 13.12:41). The consumed mechanism for DT-12's promotion path is therefore mislabelled at source, and 13.05.02:71 records that CX-M11 does not list gear-marketplace among the domains it serves — so the declared dependency points at a mechanism that neither carries a message thread nor serves this domain. The disclosure behaviour itself is specified (13.02.02:101, DT-12 at :131, D-10), so no product invention is forced; the defect is the dependency edge. Warning upheld as filed.

verdicts.claim: Three root-unit files assert 13.13's Role Lens is empty, but 13.13's Role Lens is fully populated with all four personas including a config grant to Operator.
verdicts.reason: All quotes exist, but 'empty' is defined in the same breath as 'no persona holds a manufacturer authorisation', and the populated table says exactly that. 13.13-authorized-dealer-map-pricing.md:12 reads in full '**⚠️ This feature has no persona.** None of the four — Musician, Producer, Operator, Fan — is an authorised dealer', and the table it introduces agrees: :20 '| Operator | ⚙️ Config — **poor fit** | The closest of the four, and still wrong...'; :18/:19/:21 give the other three read-only bystander rows ('finds it mildly annoying', 'a display quirk'). gear-marketplace-index.md:103 states both halves in one sentence — 'Role Lens is **empty**. No persona holds a manufacturer authorisation.' — and index:90 carries the same poor-fit Config grant. The two readings are not in conflict: no persona *fits* the dealer role, and the four are documented as encountering MAP without holding authorisation. Nor is the MoSCoW rationale factually false: index:131 and 13.13:87 place 13.13 in WONT on the ground that no persona holds a manufacturer authorisation, which the Operator row itself confirms ('and still wrong'). The failure scenario also cannot fire — 13.13 Q-02/Q-03 are both resolved by scope to WONT (13.13:87, :88), so no dealer surface is due to be shipped either way.

verdicts.claim: 13.12's Q-02 and Q-03 argue from the premise that the trader/private regime determination rides on the storefront, which Q-01 resolves against in terms.
verdicts.reason: Quotes verified (13.12-gear-seller-storefront-policies.md:215 Q-01 resolved — '01.08 D-01... it never determines it, and **it holds no per-storefront regime field**'; :216 Q-02; :217 Q-03; DT-05 unretracted at :152). But neither downstream row asserts the dead premise as true. Q-02 reports what DT-05 argues ('DT-05 argues first-class, because the regime determination needs somewhere to live') — an accurate description of :152 — and Q-03 is explicitly conditional ('**if** the regime determination rides on the storefront'), a condition Q-01 falsifies, so the conditional simply does not fire. Both sit in the same Open Questions table one and two rows *below* the resolution, which states its own 'Consequence for this file' explicitly, so an architect cannot reach Q-02 without having read the answer. Q-02 also retains independent grounds ('DT-05's two-capacities case says it may need to') and Q-03 is a presentation question settled in its policy half by D-19 (:208). Residual is an unannotated rationale, not a contradiction, and no build diverges.

verdicts.claim: Four deferral markers in the 13.01 CX file have no owner and an expired target, one declaring a conflict that needs the owner — all four resolved by the [DEEP] children.
verdicts.reason: The four markers exist as quoted (13.01-canonical-gear-catalog-cx.md:33, :69, :84, :94), and the finding concedes 'Nothing product-level'. Every one is answered in a sibling that names the CX item it closes, which is rule 3 on its face: 13.01.02-catalog-contribution-moderation.md:154 'This resolves the open rejection-behaviour item in CX-01 §2'; :163 'This resolves the open item in CX-03 §5'; 13.01.01-model-records-taxonomy-attributes.md:91 and D-10 (:175) 'Resolves CX-04's schema-backfill question'; 13.01.01 D-07 (:172) 'Resolves the CX-05 conflict the CX file flagged as needing the owner' — reinforced at 13.01.01:152 and by 13.01.02:157 ('This resolves the CX-05 conflict without contradicting D-01'). The named failure (a downstream pass implementing a publish block for safety attributes) is foreclosed by D-07's asymmetric-trust rule, which preserves both 13.01.02 D-01 and 13.01.05 D-01. Stale marker text in the pair file is a writeback-hygiene residue, not a missing decision.

verdicts.claim: Two ownerless deferral markers in the 13.02 CX file point at a completed stage; both already resolved by children that name the CX item.
verdicts.reason: Markers verified (13.02-condition-originality-disclosure-cx.md:35, :50) and, as the finding concedes, nothing product-level is missing. Both answers are one file over with explicit back-references: 13.02.01-condition-grading-scale.md:102 E-11 handles 'Seller edits a flaw on a live listing, invalidating the published grade (CX-01's open item)' — edit blocked, 'the *listing* never stalls and never auto-downgrades' — locked as D-09 (:187) and D-03 (:181), and :152 states 'Reconciles **CX-01's open synthesis item**'; 13.02.02-mandatory-flaw-disclosure.md:173 D-11 'Resolves CX-02's synthesis question 5.' The Step-6 writeback the sub-domain CX file lacks did land at domain level — gear-marketplace-cx.md:302 records 'a later edit is *challenged*, never the listing (no auto-downgrade, no stall — domain D-03 intact, E-11/D-09)'. verdicts.claim: Two deferral markers in the 13.04 CX file have no owner, point at a completed stage, and no tracked question anywhere covers them.
verdicts.reason: Markers verified verbatim (13.04-price-discovery-market-data-cx.md:34 merge recompute flipping a bucket; :68 bucket crossing threshold mid-run), and no Q row covers them — but both subjects are already owned. gear-marketplace-cx.md:397 routes them by name: 'Price-guide comp aggregation & materialisation pipeline | `/create-prd-architecture` | 13.04.01 owns what is shown and when. Batch vs. streaming, materialised views, **recompute-on-merge** are architecture' — which is marker 1's subject, with per-run snapshot pinning squarely inside materialisation; 13.04.01-price-guide-comps.md:25 makes the same split ('the aggregation and materialisation pipeline is architecture (routed to `/create-prd-architecture`)'). The product-visible half is fixed: what a page renders is a pure function of the current confidence state per 13.04.03:51-57 States and Happy Path :31-33, so a page that quoted yesterday and refuses today renders the Partial state ('Raw comps as examples; no median, no suggestion'), and per-listing skip semantics for fleet runs are already the established pattern at 13.04.02:40 ('Listing skipped with reason'). No invention forced.

verdicts.claim: 13.05.02 makes bids ascending and binding but never states the minimum bid increment or the permitted auction durations, and no tracked question owns either.
verdicts.reason: Verified by exhaustive search, not just by reading the file: the string 'increment' does not appear anywhere in 13-gear-marketplace except 13.05.01-offers-counter-offers.md:158 (a re-offer step, not a bid step), and 'duration' appears in the sub-domain only at 13.05.02-auctions-bidding.md:27 'Seller lists as an auction with start price, reserve and duration' — never enumerated. Behavior:23 'Bids are ascending and binding' is the only rule stated. Not tracked: 13.05.02 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 (:86-88) cover feature existence, anti-snipe extension and real-time bid state; sub-domain index Q-01/Q-02 (:46-47) cover binding acceptance and market culture; the sub-domain CX file fixes nothing. Not downstream detail by this tree's own standard — the sibling offer feature fixes the equivalent numbers at this layer (13.05.01:146 D-06 '48h, seller-configurable 24h–7d... Max 6 moves', :158 D-18 '≥5% of asking'), as does 13.12 with seeded ranges. Divergence is real and user-visible: 'any raise above the standing bid' versus a percentage band produce different endgames, and 13.05.02:19 names the Fan as 'Most at risk... least ability to walk away'. Warning, not blocking — the feature sits behind an unresolved [OWNER] existence question (Q-01, COULD).

verdicts.reason: REFUTED on the tracking claim, which is factually wrong. 13.05.01-offers-counter-offers.md:172 Q-05 covers both halves verbatim: '**Is a second-chance offer binding on the underbidder** (CX-03)? verdicts.claim: 13.07.02's States table specifies an 'estimate' rendering that its own D-01/D-02 prohibit, leaving whether the state is implemented unresolved.
verdicts.reason: The row is quoted correctly but read against its own text. 13.07.02-international-customs-landed-cost.md:55 reads '| Partial | Estimated, not guaranteed | Explicit "estimate" framing — **and per DT-01, this is the failure mode, not a feature** |' — the cell disqualifies itself in the same breath, so it documents a rejected option rather than specifying a state. That reading is locked three ways in the same file: D-01 (:80) 'A quoted landed cost is a commitment, not an estimate', D-02 (:81) 'If a border can't be quoted reliably, don't sell across it', and the Error row (:54) 'Must not fall through to an un-quoted international sale'. D-06 (:85) then makes the engine a per-destination time-bounded ruleset precisely so the estimate branch is unnecessary. No competent implementer builds a state annotated 'not a feature' against three decisions forbidding it; keeping a rejected option in a States table is a presentation flaw, not ambiguity.

verdicts.claim: The parcel/freight envelope is stated only approximately, so both the classification boundary and the override-abuse test are untestable, and no question owns the numbers.
verdicts.reason: The '~30kg / ~150cm / palletised' quote is accurate (13.07.01-freight-oversize-packing.md:25) but the same sentence assigns the number away from product: 'The threshold is a physical fact of the carrier network, not a WeJammin policy' — i.e. it is read from the CX-M14 carrier integration this file explicitly does not own (:23 'It does not own the carrier account, label generation, or tracking — those are the cross-cut's'). Two builds on the same carrier account get the same answer, so the 29kg-combo divergence does not arise from the spec. The override-abuse half is a misreading: :51 keys the flag to the model record, not the approximation — 'Classification is derived from the catalog model, not free-typed per listing — **an override below the model's known envelope is flagged**' — which is exactly testable (declared value < catalog model value), and :47 covers the no-dimensions case separately. The genuinely open items in this file are owned as Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 (:96-98).

verdicts.claim: 13.09.02 gives three different answers to who authors a consigned listing's disclosure (Behavior, an Edge Case, and D-03).
verdicts.reason: One answer, plus a pointer to it, plus loose prose consistent with it. D-03 (13.09.02-consignment-sales-custody.md:79) locks it: 'The consignor signs the disclosure; the consignee transcribes'. The edge case at :40 is not an open question — its cell is 'Who signs the disclosure? See DT-01', and DT-01 (:59) reaches D-03's answer in terms ('Either the consignor must sign the disclosure (and the consignee merely transcribes), or... **The first is correct and needs designing**'). Behavior:23 'The consignee lists, **discloses** (13.02 — on someone else's object)' is compatible with transcription and flags the anomaly in its own parenthetical; it makes no claim about who signs. Cross-Cut Notes :66 repeats the DT-01 framing. An implementer building the flow reads the Decisions table, which is unambiguous, so 13.02.03 D-03's signer-carries-liability rule is not silently broken.

verdicts.claim: Two inline deferral markers in 13.09 carry no owner and one carries no target at all; neither is covered by any tracked question.
verdicts.reason: Partially upheld and narrowed. Verified: 13.09.01-tradein-part-exchange.md:41 '| Owner trades in gear with an outstanding layaway or lien | They don't fully own it | `[PENDING]` — the chain (13.06.05) would know |' is a bare marker with no owner and no target — malformed tracking, and uncovered by 13.09.01 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 (:85-87, which are margin exposure, return shipping, dealer persona). No answer exists elsewhere for the product behaviour: 13.06.05-ownership-transfer-on-settlement.md:58-59 governs only the chain write on a non-owner transfer ('prior tenure — unrecorded'; must not attach where another party holds an active claim), not whether intake accepts, warns or blocks — and 13.09.01 D-01 (:77) makes a trade-in two ownership transfers, so an encumbered unit reaches the transfer path. Divergence (block vs warn-and-record) is plausible. The second marker is REFUTED: 13.09.03-inspection-intake-grading.md:47's contradiction case is answered in its own file by D-02 (:82) 'The intake grade is recorded *alongside* the owner's claim, never replacing it... let the evidence arbitrate', D-04 (:83) 'Ignorance and concealment are not distinguished', and D-05 (:85) pre-fill-never-auto-assert. Warning stands on the layaway/lien marker alone.

verdicts.claim: Two 13.10 decisions state normative defaults only qualitatively ('defaults conservative', 'bounded and short') and no question owns either number.
verdicts.reason: Quotes verified (13.10.02-rental-availability-reservation.md:79 D-02, :39; 13.10.03-deposits-damage-return-condition.md:82 D-04, :54) and no Q row owns the numbers — but the divergence claimed is not available. The assessment window carries a stated magnitude in the same file: 13.10.03:39 'Assessment window is **minutes at a loading dock, not days**', which excludes the finding's own build-B (48 hours) as non-conforming, leaving a narrow band. The turnaround buffer is by decision a lender-configurable field ('configurable and defaults conservative'), so the contested value is a launch default for a per-lender setting rather than a product rule, and the renter-visible behaviour (a unit returned Monday is not rentable Monday) is fixed either way. Proportionality also cuts against: all three 13.10 features sit in the MoSCoW WONT bucket (recorded at gear-marketplace-index.md:130), so unseeded defaults on an out-of-launch sub-domain are not a forced invention at this layer.
